An AI-generated advertisement impersonating attorney Leal drew Hernandez into payment and disclosure of residency and identity documents on a false professional-relationship basis.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable materialised physical health and safety impact; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

In the originating interview, Hernandez said he had not slept for two days and stayed focused on his phone awaiting further messages. He expressed fear because the scammers held his documents and described later extortion demands. This supports meaningful but bounded sleep disturbance linked to the synthetic entry advertisement and subsequent fraud course. No clinical diagnosis, baseline comparison or minimum duration is required. The source does not establish psychiatric crisis or irreversible impairment.
The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable materialised rights and liberty impact; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.
The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable materialised equal treatment and non-discrimination impact; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

Hernandez reported sending his Social Security and residency documents after the synthetic attorney advertisement induced contact and further requests. These are protected identifiers with material access consequences for one person, supporting meaningful bounded confidentiality loss. Future identity misuse and catastrophic non-restorability are not inferred from his understandable concerns.

Hernandez reported paying US$4,820 and then falling behind on rent and owing two months of electricity because he spent his money on the scheme. These are actual impaired household obligations. The below-US$10,000 S1 criterion expressly excludes material livelihood impairment. The amount paid is known, but the full livelihood consequence has no defensible aggregate USD valuation. The alternative S3 material-but-bounded livelihood-loss criterion applies. S2 alone understates the realised impairment of housing and utility payments. Eviction, shut-off, insolvency and widespread economic loss are not reported and do not support S4.
